discoveries.choice: notes.txt holds exactly one short plain-text line ("one line of notes") instead of a structured or multi-line document.
discoveries.whyItMatters: The phase goal is to have a notes file whose content the reader can consume; choosing free-form prose fixes the file's shape, so any later tooling that expects headings, bullets, or key/value lines would find nothing to parse and the file's meaning rests entirely on one human-readable sentence.

alternatives.option: Write several lines of notes, e.g. a bulleted list of items
alternatives.consequence: Gives more information per file and supports per-item parsing, but invents content and structure the phase did not ask for.

alternatives.option: Write the line in a structured machine-readable format such as JSON or YAML
alternatives.consequence: Enables automated consumption, but adds schema and quoting concerns and makes the file unreadable as a plain note.

recommendation.choice: Keep a single plain-text line of notes.
recommendation.reason: It satisfies the minimal requirement of a readable notes file without committing the phase to an invented schema or extra content.
